subject: history_social
notes: Mehrgarh is an archaeological site in Balochistan, Pakistan.
People lived there from about 7000 BCE, making it one of the earliest farming settlements in South Asia.
Its inhabitants grew barley and wheat and raised cattle, sheep, and goats.
Molars from burials dated to roughly 9,000 to 7,500 years ago contain small, neatly drilled holes.
Researchers concluded that the holes were made with flint-tipped drills in living people, an early form of dentistry.
stem: The student wants to present the dental finding from Mehrgarh and explain its significance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Mehrgarh, in Balochistan, Pakistan, was settled around 7000 BCE and is one of the earliest farming settlements in South Asia.
choices.B: The early farmers of Mehrgarh grew barley and wheat and raised cattle, sheep, and goats from around 7000 BCE onward.
choices.C: At Mehrgarh, an early farming settlement in Balochistan, molars from burials dated to roughly 9,000 to 7,500 years ago contain small, neatly drilled holes.
choices.D: Small holes drilled into molars from Mehrgarh, roughly 7,500 to 9,000 years old, appear to be an early form of dentistry on living people.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: state the finding (drilled holes in ancient molars) and explain why it matters (it is evidence of early dentistry on living people). Only one choice does both.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It describes the site's age and importance for farming but says nothing about the dental finding.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It describes the inhabitants' farming, which is unrelated to the dental finding.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It reports the finding accurately but does not say what the holes mean. It is the closest near miss because it covers half the goal.
explanation.D: Correct. It presents the drilled molars and explains their significance as an early form of dentistry.
